skill.name: twitter-automation
skill.description: Automate Twitter/X posting, media posts, likes, retweets, direct messages, follows, and profile lookups through the inference.sh belt CLI.
skill.summary: Run common Twitter/X account actions through inference.sh CLI app commands.
skill.author: inference-skills

security_audit.summary: The markdown backtick detector produced many false positives on tables and code-fence markers, but several shell examples are real external commands that can post, delete, like, retweet, DM, follow users, and install remote skills. Hardcoded URLs are mostly documentation or examples, while the main concern is broad CLI authority over a Twitter/X account and potential social platform abuse.

remediation.issue: Broad belt CLI permission can run any belt subcommand from this skill.
remediation.suggestion: Narrow allowed tools to the specific app commands needed, or require explicit user confirmation before any state-changing post, delete, DM, like, retweet, or follow action.

remediation.issue: Examples include visible and irreversible social account actions.
remediation.suggestion: Add safety guidance that previews exact content, target accounts, and action type before execution, and discourage bulk or unsolicited engagement automation.

remediation.issue: Related-skill installation examples use npx to fetch remote packages.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer marketplace installation instructions with trusted source verification, pinned references, and warnings about installing third-party skills.

semantic_findings.title: Broad Twitter/X Account Action Permission
semantic_findings.description: The skill declares allowed-tools: Bash(belt *) and then documents commands for posting, deleting posts, liking, retweeting, sending DMs, and following users. This grants broad account-changing capability through one CLI namespace, so accidental or malicious prompts could perform visible social actions if the user approves the skill.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The permission and documented app list directly show broad remote account actions. The risk is contextual rather than a single syntax pattern.

semantic_findings.title: Potential Social Platform Abuse Workflows
semantic_findings.description: The skill description explicitly lists engagement bots and audience growth, while examples include liking, retweeting, DMs, and following users. These capabilities can support spam or unwanted outreach if used without strict user confirmation and platform-policy checks.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The stated use cases and examples clearly include engagement automation. Legitimate social media management is possible, but abuse risk is inherent in the documented workflows.

content.value_statement: Managing Twitter/X tasks manually slows down social media workflows. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code guided commands for posting, engagement, messages, and profile lookups through inference.sh.
actual_capabilities: Posts text tweets through the x/post-tweet app.
Creates posts with media URLs through x/post-create.
Likes, retweets, deletes, and retrieves posts by tweet ID.
Sends direct messages to a recipient ID.
Follows users and retrieves user profiles by username.
Shows workflows for generating media with inference.sh apps before posting.
limitations: Requires the inference.sh belt CLI and a logged-in account.
Requires a configured Twitter/X integration with appropriate permissions.
Does not include bulk scheduling, rate-limit management, or approval queues.
Can perform visible account actions, so users must review every command before execution.

use_cases.title: Publish product updates
use_cases.description: Prepare and post concise launch updates or feature announcements from a terminal workflow.

use_cases.title: Share generated media
use_cases.description: Create an image or video with inference.sh apps and post the resulting media URL to Twitter/X.

use_cases.title: Review account interactions
use_cases.description: Retrieve post details or user profiles before deciding whether to engage from an authorized account.

prompt_templates.title: Post a simple update
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a single text tweet.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the twitter-automation skill to post this update after showing me the exact command: <tweet text>.

prompt_templates.title: Create a media post
prompt_templates.scenario: Post prepared text with an existing image or video URL.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Twitter/X automation skill to create a post with this text and media URL. Ask for confirmation before running it.

prompt_templates.title: Check a user before engaging
prompt_templates.scenario: Look up a profile before follow or message actions.
prompt_templates.prompt: Get the Twitter/X profile for <username> and summarize the result. Do not follow or message the user unless I confirm.

prompt_templates.title: Build a guarded posting workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow with generated media and approval gates.
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate media with inference.sh, draft a Twitter/X post, show the final text and media URL, then wait for my approval before posting.

output_examples.input: Post a short update about our new API documentation.
output_examples.output: The assistant drafts a concise tweet, shows the belt command that will publish it, and asks for confirmation before posting.
The assistant runs the profile lookup command and returns key profile details without taking any engagement action.

output_examples.input: Share this image URL with a caption.
output_examples.output: The assistant prepares a media post command using the supplied URL and asks the user to approve the exact caption and media link.

best_practices: Preview every post, DM, follow, like, retweet, or delete action before running it.
Use authorized accounts and follow Twitter/X platform rules for automation and outreach.
Keep credentials and integration setup outside prompts and command examples.
anti_patterns: Do not run bulk engagement, spam, or unsolicited DM campaigns.
Do not post generated media without checking ownership, consent, and accuracy.
Do not install related skills or remote packages without verifying the source.

faq.question: Does this skill post directly to Twitter/X?
faq.answer: Yes. It uses inference.sh belt commands that can publish posts when the account integration is configured.

faq.question: Can it send direct messages?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill documents an x/dm-send command that sends a message to a recipient ID.

faq.question: Does it support images or videos?
faq.answer: Yes. It uses x/post-create with a media URL and includes workflows for generated images and videos.

faq.question: Do I need an inference.sh account?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples require the belt CLI and a login before commands can run.

faq.question: Is this safe for automated engagement?
faq.answer: Use caution. The skill can like, retweet, DM, and follow, so every action should require explicit review.

faq.question: Can Claude Code use this skill?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.
